chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I asked Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man who is in tawaf, having completed part of it while part of it remains upon him, so he leaves the tawaf to go to al-Ḥijr or to part of the mosque, if he has not performed the Witr, and then performs Witr, then returns and completes his tawaf. Do you consider that better, or should he complete the tawaf and then perform Witr, even if some brightness of dawn has appeared?
So he said: "Begin with the Witr and interrupt the tawaf if you fear [missing it], then come back to the tawaf."

key_terms.أَسْفَرَ: the dawn became bright or daylight began to spread
key_terms.الطَّوَافِ: the ritual circumambulation around the Kaʿbah
key_terms.الْحِجْرِ: al-Ḥijr, the area adjacent to the Kaʿbah
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, here referring to al-Masjid al-Ḥarām
key_terms.الْوَتْرِ: the Witr prayer performed in the night prayer sequence

ai.seo_question: If I am in the middle of tawaf and fear missing Witr prayer, should I stop tawaf to pray Witr first?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a person whose tawaf is interrupted by concern over missing the time of Witr prayer. Imam Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام instructs that if one fears missing Witr, he should interrupt tawaf, perform Witr, and then return to complete the tawaf.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2796 - It is narrated from Abdurrahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (as) about a man who is performing tawaf and has completed part of it, with some still remaining, but he leaves the tawaf to go to al-Hijr or another part of the mosque to perform the Witr prayer if he has not yet prayed it. Then he returns to complete his tawaf. Should he do this, or is it better to complete the tawaf first and then perform Witr, even if the time for Witr is nearing its end?
Imam (as) said: "Start with Witr and interrupt the tawaf if you fear missing it, then return to complete your tawaf."
